key_insight: GEAR trains the image tokenizer and autoregressive generator together instead of separately, so the tokenizer learns representations that are easier for the generator to model. This end-to-end guidance improves the alignment between compression and generation.
problem_solved: Most visual generative pipelines use a two-stage setup where a tokenizer is trained first and then frozen before generator training. This decoupling can produce latents that reconstruct well but are not ideal for the generator, limiting synthesis quality and efficiency.
method: Jointly train a vector-quantized (VQ) tokenizer and an autoregressive (AR) generator in an end-to-end loop.
Use representation alignment as guidance so the tokenizer adapts to what the generator can model effectively.
Replace the fixed tokenizer + generator pipeline with a co-optimized system for image synthesis.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, GEAR offers a more integrated way to build image generation systems that can improve training efficiency and generation quality. It is especially relevant for anyone working with discrete latent image models, tokenizers, or autoregressive synthesis.
visual_elements: Before/after pipeline diagram comparing two-stage training vs. end-to-end GEAR

Simple icon set for reconstruction, compression, and generation to show the role of each component
Side-by-side performance plot or quality tradeoff chart illustrating improved alignment
paper_title: GEAR: Guided End-to-End AutoRegression for Image Synthesis
paper_authors: Bin Lin, Zheyuan Liu, Chenguo Lin, Sixiang Chen, Yunyang Ge
